questions.text: Which Owner-funded input is source-backed by 401-402?

options.text: Site information, surveys, tests, and required specialty services are Owner responsibilities when needed.
The Architect must personally finance all soil tests.
The contractor must pay the Architect's income tax.
The PRC supplies the project survey.

questions.rationale: The owner-responsibility section requires the Owner to provide or pay for project information, tests, and required specialty services.
questions.explanation: Treats Additional Services as included; renderings and detailed cost estimating beyond CD requirements are expressly listed as Additional Services requiring separate authorization. Applies wrong rate and ignores authorization requirement; Additional Services require written authorization and are typically billed at a rate different from CA hourly rate. Inappropriately refuses to perform services; renderings and estimating are within architectural practice; the issue is whether they are authorized as Additional Services, not whether the architect may provide them. When the Owner requests work that appears to be Additional Services, the architect should immediately notify the Owner in writing, identifying the service, estimating the cost or hourly commitment, and requesting authorization before proceeding. Before providing unrequested Additional Services, the architect must issue written notice identifying scope, estimating cost, and requesting written authorization.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, what is required when the Architect renders additional services?

options.text: Additional compensation is required.
The work becomes free if requested by the Owner.
The contractor pays the Architect directly.
The service is converted to a guarantee bond.

questions.rationale: SPP 202 states that additional services require additional compensation.

questions.text: Which phase is part of the checked basic services structure?

options.text: Design Development Phase.
Guarantee bond posting.
CPD provider accreditation.
Contractor bankruptcy adjudication.

questions.rationale: The 401-402 agreement lists design development as one of the Architect's basic services.

questions.text: Which service is excluded by the checked 401-402 agreement notes?

options.text: Full-time Construction Supervision.
Schematic design studies.
Design development drawings.
Contract documents services.

questions.rationale: The 401-402 notes say the agreement does not cover Fulltime Construction Supervision.

questions.text: Which presentation-related service is separately paid under the checked source when necessary and approved?

options.text: Scale models, 3D models, or walkthrough presentations.
A PRC professional ID card.
The contractor's guarantee warranty.
A bid bond supplied by the contractor.

questions.rationale: SPP 202 treats scale models, 3D models, and walkthrough presentations as separately paid with Owner approval and coordination fee.

questions.text: When does SPP 202 allow per diem plus travel and living expenses to be charged to the Owner?

options.text: When the Architect or authorized representative must perform services beyond 50.0 kilometers from the established office.
Whenever the project is in the same building as the Architect's office.
Only when a contractor default occurs.
Only after final payment to the contractor.

questions.rationale: The source sets a 50.0-kilometer distance trigger for per diem plus travel and living expenses.

questions.text: How are acoustic or illumination specialists treated in the checked SPP 202 source?

options.text: They are recommended by the Architect for Owner approval, paid separately by the Owner, and subject to a coordination fee.
They are always included in the Architect's basic fee without coordination fee.
They replace the Architect as the owner's representative.
They are paid only from contractor retention.

questions.rationale: The source lists specialist services as separately paid services with Owner approval and a coordination fee.

questions.text: Who pays for extra sets of contract documents under SPP 202?

options.text: The Owner.
The PRC Board automatically.
The lowest bidder only.
The Architect without compensation in all cases.

questions.rationale: SPP 202 says the Owner pays the Architect for additional sets of contract documents.

questions.text: What is the source-safe treatment of owner-ordered changes after approval?

options.text: The Owner pays for extra time, resources, drafting, or other office expenses.
They are always absorbed into the basic fee.
They are illegal once schematic design is complete.
They are payable only as CPD credits.

questions.rationale: SPP 202 makes post-approval owner changes separately compensable.

questions.text: Which answer best separates basic from extra work?

options.text: Check whether the task is a listed basic phase duty, additional service, separately paid service, reimbursable, or excluded service.
Treat every client request as free basic work.
Treat every site visit as a contractor bond issue.
Use only the article title and ignore the service source.

questions.rationale: The source-safe approach classifies the task by source category before answering.
